sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate now faithfully encodes the requirement: it targets ship, requires the ship-owned iceClass and LIWL inputs with canonical datatypes, preserves IA/IA Super applicability, requires explicit practicability evidence, and correctly branches to either an ice knife extending below the LIWL or an equivalent rudder-protection means without imposing both alternative classes. Deterministic validation is valid and no vocabulary repair is needed.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Reject: the candidate omits the declared required input nltl:lowerIceWaterline (LIWL) entirely, despite the requirement and dependency inputs identifying LIWL as required. Add a ship-owned nltl:lowerIceWaterline property constraint with its canonical xsd:string datatype and required presence, while retaining the direct nltl:extendsBelowLowerIceWaterline check on the ice-knife node. Preserve the existing IA/IA Super applicability and practicability alternatives.

Reject the conjunctive equivalent-means branch. In the iceKnifePracticable=false alternative, the nested arrangement node currently must simultaneously satisfy sh:class nltl:rudderProtectionArrangement and sh:class nltl:equivalentRudderProtectionMeans; encode the equivalent protection alternative as the required equivalent-means class (or an explicitly correct alternative), rather than imposing both class constraints. Preserve the ship-owned nltl:lowerIceWaterline xsd:string presence constraint and the existing IA/IA Super applicability and practicability alternatives. No vocabulary matcher is needed because all required canonical terms are supplied.

The candidate now faithfully encodes the requirement: it targets ship, requires the ship-owned iceClass and LIWL inputs with canonical datatypes, preserves IA/IA Super applicability, requires explicit practicability evidence, and correctly branches to either an ice knife extending below the LIWL or an equivalent rudder-protection means without imposing both alternative classes. Deterministic validation is valid and no vocabulary repair is needed.
